To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a method for exploration by using temporal difference error as a secondary reward in deep reinforcement learning that is faster than other state-of-the art methods on a variety of tasks.

we propose an exploration method that encourages exploration in sparse reward landscapes by maximizing the absolute value of TD error, that is based on an adversarial Q learning framework, and that is able to achieve state of the art performance on a set continuous control benchmark tasks.

(i) we propose a method to encourage exploration in deep RL that is based on the temporal difference error of the Q-value function, (ii) our method is inspired by dopaminergic reward prediction error in the brain that influences animal behavior, (iii) we demonstrate that our method performs comparably or faster than state-of-the-art methods on a set of benchmark tasks, and (iv) we provide a detailed analysis of our method in terms of exploration behavior and convergence speed.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a new exploration objective for deep reinforcement learning that is based on the temporal difference error, and that we show that this objective outperforms state-of-the-art methods on a set of challenging continuous control tasks.

we provide a principled approach for incorporating the temporal difference error into the exploration objective, which can accelerate the convergence of the deep reinforcement learning agent in a variety of tasks.
we introduce a novel secondary reward signal for reinforcement learning, and demonstrate the effectiveness of this signal in accelerating exploration.

exploration can be improved by leveraging the TD-error of the Q-function, and this can be done in an efficient off-policy manner.
